prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1406; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant's attorney, who reports a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection involving the insured's vehicle. The attorney states the claimant has neck and back pain and is represented going forward.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver listed on the policy was operating the insured vehicle at the time of loss, and the policy was in force with no gaps in coverage. No indication the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It places the claimant's vehicle in the stopped lane at the time of impact and records the other driver's account, which matches the claimant's statement.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses gave statements describing the impact the same way the claimant and the other driver did. Scene photos reviewed and consistent with the described collision.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. Rear bumper, trunk lid and tail lamp damage is consistent with the force of the reported impact. A few older scratches near the bumper may predate this loss and have been noted separately for the estimate.

Entry 6: Claimant's attorney provided the medical summary. Reported injuries are neck and back strain, which fit the type and force of a rear-end impact of this kind.

Entry 7: Records show no prior treatment to the neck or back area in the records reviewed so far. Requested prior claim history to confirm.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication. Provider notes show steady improvement, and visits have tapered as the claimant recovers.

Entry 9: Claimant has given the same account of the collision in each contact, including the attorney's correspondence, the recorded statement and the medical intake forms.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file. The accident, the claimant's presence in the vehicle, the damage and the injury pattern all line up, so the claim is proceeding under standard handling with the attorney as point of contact.
